sections.title: Frame. Assemble. Run. Learn.
body: Four connected stages. Your team holds the business context and approval decisions; IRG connects the creator and operating work.

hero.title: From creator fit to campaign impact.
hero.body: One operating model connects creator access, campaign operations and performance learning.
hero.context: Travel, hospitality and lifestyle each need a clear brief. Who needs to care? What makes the experience distinctive? What must the campaign achieve? Those answers guide creator decisions, coordinated delivery and the next step.

sections.title: The right shortlist starts before outreach.
body: Audience, setting, creative approach and brand suitability are considered together. Reach is one part of the decision. IRG turns the brief into selection criteria and records why each creator belongs on the shortlist.

items.title: Audience fit
items.body: Who the creator reaches and why that audience matters to this brief.

items.title: Brand suitability
items.body: The tone, context and content that support a credible relationship.

items.title: Creative opportunity

sections.input: Business priorities, audience context, brand guidance and non-negotiable requirements.
sections.output: A considered shortlist with rationale, relevant context and questions to resolve before outreach.

sections.title: Good work needs a clear path to delivery.

items.title: Coordinate

items.title: Approve

items.title: Deliver

sections.title: Reporting should change the next decision.
body: Read the evidence against the objective. Explain what to repeat, what to change and what needs another test. A performance review separates observations from possible explanations.

items.title: Observe
items.body: Gather available content and campaign signals, including where evidence is incomplete.

items.title: Interpret
items.body: Consider creator fit, format, timing and market context without implying causation that the data does not establish.

items.title: Apply
items.body: Recommend what to retain, refine or test, then carry that rationale into selection and briefing.

sections.input: The agreed objective, available platform or business context and questions for the next campaign.
sections.output: A performance review with observations, limitations and recommendations.

sections.title: Agree the scope around the work you need.

Creator access, operations and learning describe connected capabilities. The agreed engagement determines the deliverables, responsibilities and activity; this page does not imply every capability is sold separately.

sections.title: Questions to resolve together.
body: Use these points to evaluate the proposed engagement and identify what needs agreement. They are planning questions, not universal contract terms or unverified claims about every campaign.

items.title: Creator suitability
items.body: Which audience, content and brand-suitability checks belong in this brief, and what evidence is available for each recommendation?

items.title: Approval ownership
items.body: Who can approve creators, creative and publication? How will consolidated feedback and approval decisions be recorded?

items.title: Content rights
items.body: Which uses, channels, markets and duration need to be agreed? Is paid usage required, and who confirms the permissions?

items.title: Sponsorship disclosure
items.body: Which disclosure requirements apply to the proposed activity, and who reviews them before publication?

items.title: Reporting ownership
items.body: Who supplies each data source, which definitions will be used, and what limitations should accompany the report?

items.title: Escalation and procurement
items.body: Who is the decision-maker if timing, content or scope changes? Which procurement steps and contracts must be agreed before work starts?

links.label: Discuss scope or procurement requirements
links.linkReason: Supports the next buyer decision in Questions to resolve together.

items.title: What does IRG manage?
items.body: Creator access, campaign operations and performance learning stay connected. The agreed engagement defines the shortlist, briefs, coordination, delivery records and review your team needs.

items.title: How do you choose creators?
items.body: IRG considers audience fit, brand suitability and the creative opportunity together. Reach is one signal. The shortlist records why a creator belongs in the brief.

items.title: How do you measure performance?
items.body: We read the available content and campaign signals against the agreed objective, explain limitations and recommend what to retain, refine or test. Views and reach are not automatically evidence of sales.

items.title: Can you work with our in-house team?
items.body: Yes. Your team holds the business context, internal alignment and approval decisions. IRG connects creator recommendations, coordination, delivery records and interpretation.

items.title: Do we need a finished brief?
items.body: A live brief is useful, but not required. Share the audience problem, operating challenge or performance ambition, along with markets and timing where known.

items.title: What is agreed before a campaign starts?
items.body: The objective, audience, scope, decision-makers, practical requirements and approval points. Rights, disclosure, reporting access and procurement requirements should also be resolved for the proposed activity.

hero.title: A connected creator programme for Holafly.

sections.title: Always-on creator collaboration.
body: Creator recommendations, planning, creative development and review stayed connected.

sections.title: From monthly bursts to a connected programme.
body: Monthly restarts, late planning, availability-led selection and product-heavy briefs interrupted continuity. Learning rarely carried forward.
IRG connected selection, planning, briefing and repeat collaboration. Retained context informed the next activation.

sections.title: Audience relevance shaped selection.
body: Audience relevance and the market brief guided selection beyond travel: comedy, family, sport and interviews.
Market context shaped creative interpretation.

steps.title: Plan ahead
steps.body: Plan activations ahead of delivery. Give creators and the team time to develop work.

steps.title: Select for the brief
steps.body: Match creators to the audience and market brief, including formats beyond travel.

steps.title: Refresh the creative
steps.body: Adapt problem → emotion → product → resolution to the creator and audience.

steps.title: Retain context
steps.body: Carry creator rationale and observations into repeat collaboration and the next brief.

sections.title: Creative interpretation in the programme.
body: The creator’s format framed a familiar travel situation, showing the problem before the product’s role.

pages.reviewType: Repository content and claim-scope review; not a named expert endorsement

hero.title: Meet the traveller in the right moment.
hero.body: Travel creator work needs more than a destination backdrop. Start with the audience, the situation and the useful role your product or experience can play.

sections.title: From travel context to a creator decision.
body: For a travel brand, the brief should connect the commercial ambition with the traveller’s real situation. Decide who needs to care and what the creator can make understandable or relevant.

The Holafly programme offers one specific example: revised briefs moved through problem, emotion, product and resolution, adapted to each creator and audience. That sequence describes the case approach, not a guaranteed formula.

items.title: Audience relevance
items.body: Which traveller or market matters, and why does this creator reach them credibly?

items.title: Product role
items.body: What problem or experience belongs in the story, without asking the creator to recite a product list?

items.title: Creative setting
items.body: Which situation makes the idea recognisable and leaves room for the creator’s own format?

sections.title: Travel proof: the Holafly programme.
body: An always-on programme across the UK, Australia, California and Saudi Arabia, with continuous sourcing, advance activation planning and repeat partnerships.

sections.title: Select for the brief, beyond the category label.
body: In the Holafly case, creator selection broadened beyond travel into comedy, family, sport and interviews, with the selection matched to the brief. The reason was audience relevance and the market brief.
For your programme, assess audience fit, brand suitability and the creative opportunity together. Category relevance should explain a recommendation, not replace the rationale.

links.label: How IRG builds a considered shortlist
links.linkReason: Supports the next buyer decision in Select for the brief, beyond the category label.

sections.title: Connect activation and the next decision.
body: Agree market priorities and practical requirements, coordinate feedback and delivery, then interpret the evidence against the objective. Retained context informs the next brief.

steps.title: Frame
steps.body: Agree the objective, audience and practical requirements before creator selection.
steps.input: Your team clarifies the business objective, constraints and decision-maker.
steps.output: An agreed brief and a clear basis for creator recommendations.
steps.decision: Confirm the brief and resolve open questions before shortlisting.
steps.owner: IRG translates the business context into creative direction and selection criteria.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.body: Build the selection around relevance, suitability and the creative opportunity.
steps.input: Your team reviews recommendations against brand priorities and flags concerns.
steps.output: A considered creator shortlist with the rationale behind each recommendation.
steps.decision: Agree creator selection and the information required before outreach.
steps.owner: IRG evaluates fit, records the rationale and coordinates selection information.

steps.title: Run
steps.body: Connect creator coordination, consolidated feedback and approved delivery.
steps.input: Your team supplies necessary information and confirms approval decisions.
steps.output: A campaign plan, decision record and the agreed deliverables.
steps.decision: Record feedback or approval before the work moves into delivery.
steps.owner: IRG coordinates creators, maintains the decision record and tracks agreed outputs.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Read the available evidence against the objective and shape the next brief.
steps.input: Your team shares available business context and the next questions to answer.
steps.output: A performance review with observations, limitations and recommendations.
steps.decision: Decide what to retain, refine or test in the next cycle.
steps.owner: IRG interprets the available signals and keeps uncertainty visible.

links.label: Inspect the full operating model
links.linkReason: Supports the next buyer decision in Connect activation and the next decision.

sections.title: Choose the evidence before interpreting the outcome.
body: Agree what a view or reach figure means for the proposed activity and what business context will be available. Organic views can show content consumption; they do not establish unique people, sales or incrementality by themselves.

Keep market targets, reporting windows and cost-comparison baselines distinct. The Holafly case shows why a programme-start cost comparison should not be mixed with an August comparison against planned cost.

hero.title: An experience worth telling. A brief worth agreeing.
hero.body: Hospitality creator activity connects the guest experience with practical delivery. Define the audience, the stay and the coverage before shortlisting.

sections.title: The property experience is part of the brief.
body: A stay, route or seasonal experience creates a different planning task from a travel product programme. Creator fit includes who the audience is, what makes the setting distinctive and how the creator can interpret it credibly.
The practical arrangements belong alongside the creative direction. Questions about dates, access, inclusions, exclusions and the on-site contact should be resolved for the actual activity.

items.title: Audience and occasion
items.body: Which audience and travel occasion is relevant to this property or experience?

items.title: Experience and setting
items.body: What should be understood about the stay, route or season?

items.title: Creator interpretation
items.body: How can the experience become relevant in the creator’s own format?

sections.title: Questions to settle before the stay.
body: These are agreement points for the proposed brief, rather than claims about established contractual terms.

items.title: Practical arrangements
items.body: What are the dates, access requirements, stay inclusions, exclusions and on-site responsibilities?

items.title: Required coverage
items.body: What must be communicated, which outputs are agreed and where does the creator have room to interpret?

items.title: Approval route
items.body: Who consolidates feedback and who can approve content or a changed requirement?

items.title: Rights and disclosure
items.body: Which uses, permissions and sponsorship requirements must be agreed before publication?

items.title: Evidence access
items.body: Which content or booking data is available, who provides it and what attribution limitations apply?

blockers.details: Existing privacy page contains draft-only text. Accurate policy wording requires the data controller identity, processing purposes, lawful bases where applicable, recipients/processors, retention, rights and contact details to be confirmed. No legal assurances have been invented.

User explicitly requires the existing unfinished resource section and download setup to remain unchanged. No resource content, hide/remove action or download rebuild is included. This is not a launch blocker for this update.

Publish the client name and source-supported working process only. Do not publish numerical results, reporting dates, market comparisons, creator metrics or spelled-out programme counts. Historical CMS evidence remains unchanged and non-public.
Leadership biographies, real team imagery, legal entity details and official profiles are not established in the supplied source. Publish only existing positioning and responsibilities.
Programme-level YouTube/Instagram capability, delivery scope and proof have not been confirmed. No platform pages are generated. A reel example does not establish the programme platform mix.
Lifestyle focus is established, but a distinct substantive sector page and client evidence are not supplied. The industry hub links lifestyle buyers to creator selection in the core Services page.

Rights, disclosure, escalation and procurement requirements are represented as questions to resolve for the engagement. No certifications, universal compliance assurances, contract terms or response-time promises are invented.
The existing integration must be retained and tested with intercepted requests or an authorised test sink. No real enquiry should be sent without user authorisation.
